name: Hexagon
//: Hexagon recognizes a closed token language (spec/lexer.md §1), so this grammar
mirrors that inventory rather than guessing. Identifier classes follow §3.1:
start class is syntax, so an uppercase-start name is a type/constructor role and a
non-uppercase-start name is a term/binder role, decided by the literal first
codepoint alone. Hard keywords are §4.1; contextual keywords (§4.2) lex as ordinary
names and are only matched here in the positions the spec lists. Constructs the
lexer rejects outright (§10) are painted invalid.illegal so the editor shows the
same errors the compiler would.

patterns.//: Before #operators: spec/lexer.md §8.2 requires `||` to be one forbidden run pointing at `or`, never two pattern bars.

spec/comments.md §3: doc-comment recognition requires `/**` followed by at least one character that is not `/`, which keeps `/**/` an ordinary empty block comment while `/*** x ***/` is a doc comment.
patterns.name: comment.block.documentation.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/comments.md §3: block comments nest.
patterns.name: comment.block.hexagon

patterns.//: begin/end rather than match, so a bidirectional control inside the comment body still gets its own scope (§3.2 prohibits them in comments too).
patterns.name: comment.line.documentation.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/comments.md §3: `*/` at depth zero is a hard error, not `*` then `/`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unmatched-comment-close.hexagon

strings.//: spec/lexer.md §6: one composite String token; may span physical newlines.
strings.name: string.quoted.double.hexagon

string-escape.//: spec/lexer.md §6.2 is the complete escape inventory; no legacy JS escapes.
string-escape.name: constant.character.escape.hexagon

//: spec/lexer.md §6.2: a `\u{...}` escape must name a Unicode scalar value —
at most U+10FFFF and never a surrogate. These run before #string-escape so a
well-formed-looking but out-of-range escape loses to the invalid rule.
Leading zeros are legal, hence the `0*`.

patterns.//: A surrogate: the whole D800-DFFF block, so the second nibble is 8 through F.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unicode-escape.hexagon

patterns.//: Above U+10FFFF.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unicode-escape.hexagon

patterns.//: More than six digits, whatever their value.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unicode-escape.hexagon

bidirectional-control.//: spec/lexer.md §3.2: literal bidirectional controls are prohibited throughout source, including comments and strings — this is the trojan-source class, so it is included in those contexts too, not only at the top level.
bidirectional-control.name: invalid.illegal.bidirectional-control.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §6.2: `\u{...}` must be 1-6 hex digits naming a scalar value.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unicode-escape.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §6.2: bare `#{` is reserved for future Debug interpolation; write `\#{`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.reserved-interpolation.hexagon

interpolation.//: spec/lexer.md §6.1: the hole is lexed recursively with the normal inventory.
interpolation.name: meta.embedded.line.hexagon

brace-group.//: Keeps a record literal's `}` inside a hole from closing the interpolation.

reserved-identifier.//: spec/lexer.md §3.2: `__hex_` is reserved for compiler-generated names.
reserved-identifier.name: invalid.illegal.reserved-identifier.hexagon

//: `extern from "specifier"` is the only extern form that opens an indented block,
and it is always top-level, so the block ends at the next line starting in
column zero. The FFI contextual keywords (spec/lexer.md §4.2) are recognized only
in here: `get`, `set`, `new`, `default` and friends are ordinary names elsewhere.
extern-from-block.name: meta.extern.hexagon

patterns.//: `enum Direction = ...` / `class Foo` — the described foreign type is uppercase-start.
`export method get(...)`, `export get status(...)`, `export static method of(...)`.
`export new(...)` constructor description, and the `default` import position.

declarations.//: Names the thing being declared. `fun` always introduces a function; `let`/`var` introduce one only when a parameter list or type-parameter list follows (stdlib/Seq.hex leans on this distinction heavily).

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §4.1 hard keywords, grouped as that section groups them.
patterns.name: keyword.control.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §4.1 word operators: Hexagon has no `&&`, `||`, or `!`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.hexagon

//: spec/lexer.md §4.2: these lex as NonUpperName and mean nothing outside their
position, so each rule pins the position. `let when = true` and `{with = 3}`
must keep reading as an ordinary binding and an ordinary field.

patterns.//: `from` is always followed by a module specifier string.
patterns.name: keyword.other.from.hexagon

patterns.//: `x as y` in imports, foreign aliases, and `p as name` patterns. Something being renamed must precede it, or `let r = as b` would read as a keyword.
`derives Eq` or `derives (Eq, Show)`, which only ever follows a declaration header's name or parameter list.
`export opaque record` / `export opaque union` only.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.hexagon

//: A match/catch arm guard. spec/pattern-matching.md §3 is emphatic that `when`
is arm syntax and never pattern syntax, so it can only follow a complete arm
pattern — never an opening `(` or a `,`, which is where `Event(when, what)`,
`(when) => ...`, `f(when, g)` and `fun schedule(when: Instant)` all put it.
Requiring the arm's `=>` later on the line is necessary but nowhere near
sufficient on its own, because TextMate cannot see bracket depth.

patterns.//: Record update `{p with x = 3}`; `{with = 3}` is a field, `{with}` a pun, and `let ok = with` an ordinary name.

numbers.//: spec/lexer.md §5. Decimal only; `_` needs a digit on both sides; `n` is BigInt.

patterns.//: `0x`/`0o`/`0b` are errors, not literals: Hexagon v1 has decimal literals only.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.numeric-base.hexagon

patterns.//: A trailing `.` with nothing literal after it: write `1.0`. `1.show()` and `1..2` are fine and must not match here.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.numeric-literal.hexagon

patterns.//: Digits joined to identifier characters: `12cats`, `1nmore`, `1efoo`, `1__0`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.numeric-literal.hexagon

patterns.//: A leading `.`: write `0.5`. The second dot of `1..2` is excluded by the lookbehind.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.numeric-literal.hexagon

//: A non-uppercase-start name applied to arguments. Also catches a constraint
member's bodyless header, which is spelled the same way. The second alternative
admits an angle-bracket type-parameter list only when a call actually follows
it (`isEmpty<a>(values)`), because spec/lexer.md §8.1 makes `<` the very same
token in a comparison — `count <= 0` must keep reading as a comparison.

parameter.//: A binder followed by its type annotation: parameters, record-type fields, and `<a: Ord>` constraint binders. `:=` is assignment, not an annotation.

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §3.2: bare `_` is its own wildcard token; `_name` is an ordinary name.
patterns.name: variable.language.wildcard.hexagon

patterns.//: An uppercase-start name before an accessor `.` is always a qualifier — a module alias or a companion (spec/modules.md §3.3, §5.3). Terms are never uppercase-start, so this cannot be a field access. `..` and `...` are single tokens (§8.1), so `A..B` is a range and its `A` is an ordinary type name.
patterns.name: entity.name.namespace.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §3.1: one scope for every uppercase-start role. Type, union case, constraint, implied type, and exception are deliberately not distinguished before parsing, so this grammar does not invent a distinction either.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.hexagon

operators.//: spec/lexer.md §8.1, ordered so maximal munch (§8.2) falls out of rule order.

invalid.//: spec/lexer.md §8.3 and §10: characters and runs with no token at all. §10's last row requires *any* invalid character to be one diagnostic, so the final rule is a negated class over the whole legal repertoire rather than a list of the forbidden characters someone thought of.

patterns.//: §8.2 special-cases these so the user is pointed at `not`, `and`, `or`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.operator.hexagon

patterns.//: spec/lexer.md §2.2: space and tab are the only horizontal whitespace. There is no invisible second spelling of an ordinary space.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.whitespace.hexagon

patterns.//: Every character outside the identifier repertoire (§3.1) and the closed punctuation inventory (§8.1). Catches `~`, `'` (§3.2: ML-style `a'` names do not exist), `%`, `^`, a lone `&`, `?`, `@`, `#`, backtick, backslash, and §11's own rejected `let 😀 = 1`. `!` is excluded here because `!=` is a real token; the rule above already claims a bare `!`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.character.hexagon

tab-indentation.//: spec/lexer.md §2.2 and §10's first row: a tab anywhere from the start of a line through its first non-whitespace character is a hard error. A tab after a token is legal, and a tab inside a string or comment is content — neither reaches this rule.
tab-indentation.name: invalid.illegal.tab-indentation.hexagon
